newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans start clean-up as Oder flood water recedes.
newsitem.headline: Germans start clean-up as Oder flood water recedes.

text.p: Soldiers started to clean up flood-hit villages and stopped sandbagging dikes along the Oder River in east Germany on Tuesday as water levels fell back steadily and the risk of mass flooding receded.

In Bonn, Chancellor Helmut Kohl said total federal government aid to the region would reach 500 million marks ($268.3 million), calling the floods there the "worst natural disaster ever faced by newly-unified Germany".
Manfred Stolpe, premier of the flood-hit state of Brandenburg, hailed the efforts of thousands of soldiers and aid workers.
"In the seventh year after unification the German nation has passed its probation test on the Oder dikes," he told a special session of the lower house of parliament.

For the first time in the two-week flood crisis in eastern Germany, soldiers who had battled round the clock to reinforce dikes protecting the low-lying Oderbruch region stopped sandbagging and even started removing the bags from some areas.
No new tears appeared in dikes overnight and water levels, which started dropping on Sunday for the first time in three weeks, had fallen by up to a metre in some areas.
President Roman Herzog, visiting the flood-stricken area, said mass flooding had been avoided on the fertile Oderbruch plain because of the "fantastic" effort of soldiers.
Kohl, announcing the aid package in parliament, said the whole country was proud of the operation, which showed that the Bundeswehr was the "army of our people".
